questions.q: In the train-station analogy from this lesson, what does an event correspond to?
options: The intercom announcement — a public broadcast other systems or people can react to
The train itself
The ticket booth
The tracks the train runs on
questions.explain: Just like an intercom announcement, an event is a public broadcast that lets outside systems know something happened — it doesn't move anything itself.

questions.q: What real keyword actually fires an event and logs it to the blockchain?
options: emit
event
log
broadcast
questions.explain: You declare an event with the event keyword, but you fire it with emit — e.g., emit Transfer(msg.sender, to, amount).

questions.q: What real benefit does marking an event parameter as `indexed` provide?
options: It allows fast searching and filtering of that parameter in event logs
It makes the parameter cost zero gas
It hides the parameter from the front end entirely
It converts the parameter into a state variable
questions.explain: Up to three parameters can be marked indexed, enabling real filtering — like finding every transfer from one specific address.

questions.q: Can a smart contract read back its own past events from inside its own code?
options: No — events are read-only and can't be accessed from inside a contract
Yes, at any time using a getter function
Only the contract's owner can read past events
Only during the constructor
questions.explain: The lesson is explicit: events are read-only from a contract's own perspective — a contract cannot access its own past events.

questions.q: Why would a front-end app listen for a Deposit event instead of repeatedly checking the balances mapping?
options: It lets the app update in real time the instant something happens, without constantly polling contract state
Events cost more gas than repeatedly checking state, so they're less efficient
Mappings can't actually be read from a front end at all
There's no real difference between the two approaches
questions.explain: Listening for events lets a DApp react immediately to real on-chain activity, rather than constantly re-checking state — which is slower and more wasteful.
